dedupe_keys.name: gsa resource security satellite derived resource footprint audit of malaysian data centres

description: GSA Resource Security is an independent audit of the physical resource footprint of data centre facilities in Malaysia, built by the civic technology group Sinar Project with support from the Global South Alliance Datafication and Democracy Fund, because operators rarely disclose facility-level figures. A computer-vision pipeline measures each facility's footprint from satellite imagery, deduplicates co-located entries into buildings, and converts footprint area into estimated power demand, annual energy, carbon emissions and water use under several water-usage-effectiveness scenarios, keeping operator-disclosed and modelled facilities apart; corridors are checked against Hansen Global Forest Change data, and a corpus of Malaysian environmental review rules and Hansard debates (2008 to 2026) is analysed. Coverage is national, per facility, as a research prototype of March to September 2026. The GitHub repository read on 2026-09-28 holds the Python pipeline, a derived dataset extract (a JSON manifest with satellite captures), a static interactive map and reports; no licence is set, and the README asks users to coordinate with Sinar Project before reuse. Caveats: geocoding fallbacks misplaced some facilities, no single power-density coefficient fits all facilities, and the code is not maintained. It supports capacity planning of electricity and water demand from data centres and exposure analysis of the digital sector. No related record exists in the catalogue for Malaysian data centres.
